goal.source_text: More downforce without going over 15 N of drag at 25 m/s. You can change the angle, span, flap and endplates. Keep the chord.

constraints.label: Drag at most 15 N at 25 m/s

assumptions: Darwin may change aoa_deg, span_mm, flap_angle_deg, endplate_height_mm; it holds chord_mm, flap_chord_frac fixed.

"You can change the angle, span, flap and endplates" is read as aoa_deg, span_mm, flap_angle_deg and endplate_height_mm being editable; flap_chord_frac is not named, so it is held at its current value of 0.3 and is not editable.
"Angle" is interpreted as the main element angle of attack (aoa_deg), since it is the only angle parameter besides flap deflection, which is listed separately as flap.
The drag limit of 15 N is applied as a hard constraint, and the design speed of 25 m/s comes from the context already given.
Held at the current value while the CAD can't change it yet: chord_mm.

design_space.name: FSAE-style rear wing

parameters.name: chord_mm
parameters.description: Total chord, main element plus flap

parameters.name: flap_chord_frac
parameters.description: Flap chord as a fraction of total chord

notes: Ranges from PLAN.md B.5; W-B owns the real solver and may narrow them before CP-B.

metric_catalog.name: downforce_n
metric_catalog.description: Downforce at the design speed (VLM + viscous correction + endplates)

metric_catalog.name: drag_n
metric_catalog.description: Total drag: induced + section profile + endplate friction

metric_catalog.name: drag_profile_n
metric_catalog.description: Section profile drag (NeuralFoil) plus endplate skin friction

metric_catalog.name: cl
metric_catalog.description: Wing lift coefficient on planform area

metric_catalog.name: stall_margin_deg
metric_catalog.description: Section stall angle minus angle of attack (negative = stalled)

metric_catalog.name: span_efficiency
metric_catalog.description: Oswald e from Prandtl lifting-line theory for the planform

payload.explanation: Span and endplate height were raised together. Downforce rose 21.6% (in range) and stall margin stayed at 4.5 deg, as predicted. Drag rose only 5.52%, just below its predicted band, and L/D rose 15.2%, above its band. Effective aspect ratio rose 27.6%, cutting induced drag 1.07%, but profile drag jumped 39.5% and offset that gain.
payload.lesson: Endplate and span gains raise downforce more than drag, but profile drag growth can erase the induced-drag benefit.

payload.explanation: Raising flap from 10 to 16 deg raised downforce 8.30% (119 to 129 N) and CL 8.30%, within the predicted 3-12%, but drag rose 27.5%, above the 4-22% range. Profile drag jumped 65.0% and induced drag 17.3%, so the extra flap loading mostly bought viscous/separation drag. L/D fell 15.1%, outside the predicted -14 to -2%. Stall margin dropped 22.2% (4.5 to 3.5 deg), which was predicted.
payload.lesson: On this wing, flap beyond about 10 deg adds drag faster than downforce; check profile drag before raising flap.

payload.rationale: Span and endplates are already at their maxima, so trimming flap (lightly loaded, costly drag per unit downforce) frees drag. Spending part of it on angle, where stall margin allows, can recover downforce under the 15 N cap.

payload.explanation: Angle up 6→8 deg and flap down 16→12 deg kept downforce nearly flat (+0.23%) while drag fell 4.13%, so L/D rose 4.54%. All four predictions matched. Profile drag dropped 16.0% from the flap trim, which outweighed a small 0.461% rise in induced drag. Stall margin fell 42.9% (3.5→2.0 deg), the cost of the extra angle, and the design stayed feasible.
payload.lesson: On this wing, trimming flap sheds profile drag cheaply; spend only as much angle as stall margin allows.

Stall margin dropped from 2.0 to 1.5 deg (-25%), so lift is saturating as flap consumes margin. L/D fell 10.5%. Directions were right; two ranges missed.

payload.explanation: Raising AoA 8→9 deg and cutting flap 16→12 deg lowered downforce 1.77% (133→131 N) and drag 8.80% (13.8→12.6 N), so L/D rose 7.71%. All four predictions matched direction and range. Profile drag fell 20.96% (4.19→3.31 N), dominating the drag cut, while induced drag fell only 3.50%. Stall margin dropped 33.3% (1.5→1.0 deg), so the flap trim cost the margin the hypothesis aimed to preserve. The verdict is rejected despite the correct predictions.
payload.lesson: Trimming flap cuts profile drag strongly, but stall margin falls fast, so check margin before trading flap for angle.

Drag and L/D predictions held. The stall margin predicted flat but dropped 33.3% (1.5 to 1.0 deg), so the flap cut apparently reduced stall margin rather than preserving it. Verdict: pivot.

message.summary: Stopping: Span (1000 mm) and endplate height (300 mm) already sit at their upper bounds, the two levers that add downforce most cheaply. Angle and flap are ruled out in the notebook: flap's drag cost is steep a.
